claim.claim-text: 1. An eddy current brake configuration comprising:

(a) a magnetic field; and (b) an electrical conductor (4); wherein the eddy current brake is configured to have a first rotating shaft (2) and the electrical conductor (4) is linked to, and rotates with, the shaft (2), wherein the magnetic field within which the electrical conductor (4) moves is formed by one or more magnets (6) situated on a housing or external element (5), said housing or external element defining a cavity inside which the shaft (2) and electrical conductor (4) move, wherein the eddy current brake is configured to have at least two rotational degrees of freedom, wherein a first primary axis of rotation (X) is angularly translated relative to at least one secondary or control axis of rotation (Y), wherein the braking action is applied to the primary axis (X), and wherein movement of the electrical conductor rotationally into or out of the magnetic field about the at least one secondary axis (Y) is used to modulate the braking action, wherein the electrical conductor (4) is located at least partially within the magnetic field when braking occurs, and wherein interaction and relative movement between the electrical conductor (4) and the magnetic field induces eddy current braking forces acting to resist movement of the electrical conductor (4) and in turn acts to resist movement of the shaft (2).
2. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in claim 1, wherein the first axis of rotation (X) and at least one second axis of rotation (Y) intersect.
3. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the first axis of rotation (X) is at an orthogonal angle to the second axis of rotation (Y).

4. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in any of claims 1 or 3, wherein the shaft (2) has a collar (3), and either one section of the collar, multiple sections of the collar, or the whole collar, is an electrical conductor.
5. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in claim 4, wherein the collar (3) rotates about a second rotation axis (Y) mounted on or about the shaft (2) itself.
6. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in claim 5, wherein collar rotation also rotates the electrical conductor (4).

7. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in claim 6, wherein the electrical conductor (4) rotates about an axis or axes (X, Y) mounted on the collar (3) and, when shaft rotation occurs; at least part of the conductive member(s) (4) rotate outward from the plane of rotation of the collar (3) about a second rotation axis or axes (Y).

8. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in claim 1, wherein the electrical conductor (4) is linked to a shaft (2) via a line and centrifugal forces acting on the electrical conductor member(s) caused by rotation of the shaft (2) urging the electrical conductor (4) to axially rotate away from the shaft (2).

9. The eddy current brake configuration as claimed in claim 8, wherein at least one bias means (14) is used to tune the axial rate of movement of the electrical conductor (4) away from the shaft axis.

11. An autobelay or self-retracting lifeline incorporating the eddy current brake configuration of any of claims 1 to 9.
